findings.title: Unparenthesized OR authorization conditions leak when composed with other WHERE clauses
findings.body: getBaseConditions returns authConditions directly when there are no filter conditions (line 75), and for org/team scopes that condition is built as `(A) OR (B)` without outer parentheses (lines 171-174 and 204-207). A caller composing it as `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND <date/status condition>` gets `(A) OR (B) AND <condition>` because AND binds tighter than OR in SQL, so the first authorization branch ignores the caller's additional condition. The old Prisma WhereInput guaranteed this OR was grouped. The returned fragment should be wrapped, e.g. Prisma.sql`(${authConditions})`, so composition is safe.

findings.title: Public findMany method is removed without migrating any call sites
findings.body: This change deletes InsightsBookingService.findMany, which previously ran bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany with the authorization and filter conditions merged into the caller's where clause, and replaces it with getBaseConditions that only returns a SQL fragment. No caller in this PR is updated to issue its own $queryRaw query, so any existing consumer of findMany breaks (TypeScript compile error / runtime 'findMany is not a function'), and former consumers that passed select/orderBy/etc. lose that behavior entirely. Call sites must be migrated in the same PR or findMany retained on top of the new conditions.

findings.title: ANY(array) authorization branches are never executed against the database
findings.body: The only test that executes SQL against Postgres is the user-scope test at lines 480-491, which exercises `userId = $1 AND teamId IS NULL`. The org and team scopes, which rely on `"teamId" = ANY(${numberArray})` and `"userId" = ANY(${numberArray})` parameter binding, are only asserted by Prisma.Sql object equality (lines 295-343). Object equality cannot detect a Postgres runtime failure or wrong typing when Prisma binds a JavaScript number array to ANY(...), so the highest-risk raw-SQL authorization paths could fail at query time while all tests pass. Add $queryRaw executions for org and team scopes.

findings.title: Caching tests were deleted while the caching behavior remains
findings.body: The PR removes the 'Caching' describe block that verified repeated getAuthorizationConditions()/getFilterConditions() calls return the cached result, but insightsBooking.ts still implements cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions (lines 84-95). There is now no coverage guarding that cache against regressions (e.g. returning stale or uncached conditions), and the deletion is unrelated to the Prisma.sql conversion since the same assertions work with SQL fragments.
